input: Draft a sponsorship proposal for my sports team

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is a full multi-tier proposal or a one-page pitch deck changes the depth, structure, and length of the document entirely.
The type of sponsor being targeted (local business, corporate brand, niche industry) determines tone, the value proposition to emphasise, and what benefits to offer.
The sport, team level (amateur, semi-pro, youth, collegiate), and audience size shape the credibility and reach figures included in the proposal.
A funding target or sponsorship tier structure determines what packages and price points to include, which is central to the proposal's commercial section.
Knowing what assets the team already has (logo, stats, photos, social media following) determines how much supporting content needs to be created vs. referenced.
The desired tone — formal corporate letter vs. passionate community pitch — affects language, structure, and how the team's story is framed throughout.

Understanding the deadline and what a successful outcome looks like (a signed sponsor, a meeting secured, a specific number of prospects reached) focuses the call-to-action and urgency in the proposal.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a Sponsorship Proposal for Sports Team
gold.taskDescription: Write a sponsorship proposal document to attract financial or in-kind support for the user's sports team.

questions.title: What sport and level does your team compete at?
questions.description: Identifies the sport, competitive level (youth, amateur, semi-pro, etc.), and approximate audience or fan base size to anchor the proposal's reach and credibility figures.

questions.title: Who is the ideal sponsor you are targeting?
questions.description: Determines whether the proposal targets a local small business, a regional brand, or a national/corporate sponsor — which shapes tone, benefit packages, and ROI framing.

questions.title: What total sponsorship amount or tier structure do you need?
questions.description: Establishes the funding goal and whether there are multiple sponsorship tiers (e.g. Gold/Silver/Bronze) so the commercial packages section can be built accurately.

questions.title: Should this be a full proposal document or a short pitch?
questions.description: Clarifies the expected format and length — a detailed multi-section proposal, a concise one-pager, or a slide deck — which determines the overall structure and depth.

questions.title: What tone should the proposal have — formal or community-driven?
questions.description: Defines whether the language should be professional and corporate, warm and community-focused, or somewhere in between, shaping how the team's story is told.

questions.title: What team assets or stats do you already have available?
questions.description: Identifies existing materials such as social media follower counts, match attendance figures, logos, photos, or past sponsor testimonials that can be incorporated directly.

questions.title: When do you need this proposal ready to send?
questions.description: Establishes the deadline and what a successful outcome looks like — securing a meeting, a signed deal, or reaching a set number of prospects — to shape urgency and the call-to-action.
